CHROMIUM: rk3399: Add new dmcfreq governor This adds an interrupt based governor for the dmc devfreq device. This allows faster response for DDR transitions and removes the polling loop. It also directly scales the frequency based on usage when it increases. This is because target DDR load is much smaller than the peak memory usage. There are three settings for the new governor. Target load, hysteresis, and down throttle ms. The target load is used when scaling the frequency. Hysteresis modifies the interrupt thresholds. The floor threshold is the target load minus hysteresis times the next lower frequency. The top threshold is the target load plus hysteresis times the current frequency. Down throttle ms is the delay between increasing the frequency and when the frequency can be lowered again. BUG=chrome-os-partner:57123 TEST=boot kevin and run: cat /sys/class/devfreq/dmc/trans_stat check that there are ddr transitions happening based on the output Change-Id: I2706d7d25ba64d2eb42bab9577f54d70888b630a Signed-off-by: Derek Basehore <dbasehore@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/431190 Reviewed-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org>

chromeos-chrome: Drop glib, dbus-glib, pango, and cairo. Make the chromeos-chrome package not depend on the glib, dbus-glib, cairo, or pango packages. use_ozone implies !use_glib, !use_cairo, and !use_pango within the Chrome build, and we set use_ozone unconditionally. Note that many Chrome OS system daemons still depend on GLib, though, and the system harfbuzz library (which Chrome dynamically links against) depends on it too. Also add a harfbuzz dependency that was indirectly pulled in and s/ChromeOS/Chrome OS/g in comments. BUG=chromium:170408,chromium:457307 TEST=verified that ldd reports that the chrome binary doesn't depend on these libraries, and did builds via a few informational pfq builders Change-Id: I0500c435ebb3e18ebebf5c054590aceae00c2148 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/431908 Commit-Ready: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Tested-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

usb: Use local static variable instead of LazyInstance LazyInstance registers AtExitManager but it is for process not shared library. It causes that destructor is called when process terminated instead of dlclose(). Local static variable will be destroyed when dlclose is called because dlclose will trigger atexit().
